_comment: Protected paths for the agent layer (Phase 4). A PR touching any of these fails the required `path-guard` check, gets a comment naming the path, and is labeled needs-input. Agents propose changes to these via issue, never make them. Matching is done by .github/scripts/path-guard.sh with bash pattern syntax as used by `[[ $file == $glob ]]` — `*` and `**` both span `/`, case-insensitive since round 5 — and BOTH the new and the previous filename of a rename are matched, so a protected file cannot be moved out of its directory to escape. Three groups: (1) the agent's own instructions and prompt templates, (2) the local-safety enforcement layer — the harness settings, the git/Claude hooks, the test preload and the pipeline/gate shell scripts that keep agents off production data, since a PR that edits its own guard is a PR that has no guard, (3) the production publishing path and the launchd plists. package.json, tsconfig.json and bun.lock are listed because package.json defines the build, typecheck and deploy entry points that the pipeline and the required ci check run (a PR could otherwise set typecheck to a no-op); scripts/redeploy.sh and scripts/phase3-weekly.sh are publishing paths beside daily-automated.sh. src/config/active-source-ids.ts is listed because it defines the population the yield canary monitors: dropping a source from it silences the canary for that source, which is a human decision. Deliberately NOT protected (the Sunday retro PR edits them): .claude/notes/**, .claude/analyst-playbook.md, exemplars/**. No root CLAUDE.md exists today; the project file is .claude/CLAUDE.md — both are listed so a future root file is covered too. No enrichment prompt-template directory exists; the docs that function as enrichment prompt templates are listed individually. Added in the security loop (round 1): .claude/commands/**, .claude/skills/** and .claude/agents/** are agent instructions that sessions load and follow, like the files in group (1); netlify/** is code deployed to production with the site (group 3); docker/** is protected ahead of first use because a container definition sets what an agent run can reach; SECURITY.md is the disclosure channel — a PR that redirects it would route vulnerability reports to someone else; .github/CODEOWNERS is listed by name although .github/** covers it, so narrowing that glob later cannot drop it; and the security tests (tests/db-guard-hook.test.ts, tests/settings-security-pins.test.ts, tests/path-guard.test.ts, tests/netlify-headers.test.ts, tests/workflow-security.test.ts, scripts/__tests__/deploy-gate.test.ts) are listed because a PR that weakens a guard could otherwise delete the matching test in the same diff and keep ci green. scripts/db-read.ts is the only database access the enrichment session is granted, so it is part of the guard layer (group 2); tests/db-read.test.ts, tests/auto-enrich-guard-selftest.test.ts, tests/docker-hardening.test.ts and tests/security/** are its and the output-safety guards' tests. Added in the security loop (round 2): the enrichment chain the unattended session is allowed to run (scripts/save-batch.ts, write-description.ts, write-tags.ts, auto-gate-check.ts), the brief that frames scraped text as untrusted data (scripts/generate-enrichment-brief.ts), and the modules those scripts and the publishing path rely on for containment and URL safety (src/utils/batch-output-path.ts, outbound-url.ts, safe-url.ts, src/ingest/allowed-senders.ts, src/validators/published-artifacts.ts, scripts/lib/chrome-path.ts; some exist only on the regular branch and are listed ahead of the merge), plus the round-2 guard tests. .github/scripts/trusted-issue-thread.sh and .github/audit-ignore.json sit under .github/**. Added in the security loop (round 4): the output-safety modules the published site depends on — the enforced CSP hash list (src/validators/inline-script-allowlist.ts), the _headers generator (src/generators/security-headers.ts), the HTML and inline-JSON escapers (src/utils/html-escape.ts, src/utils/html-json.ts) — plus the schema checks for build state read back from container-writable dist/ and data/ (src/validators/persisted-state.ts), the one sanctioned writer of events URL columns, which passes every URL through safe-url (scripts/lib/url-columns.ts) and the container CLI lockfile (docker/cli/**, listed by name although docker/** covers it), and the host-run guard's test (tests/host-run-guard.test.ts); several exist only on the regular branch and are listed ahead of the merge. Added in the security loop (round 5): matching is case-insensitive (the owner's Mac filesystem is), so `.Claude/settings.json` is refused like .claude/settings.json; the ci test-report check and its committed floor (.github/scripts/test-report-check.sh, test-report-floor.json — a PR must not be able to lower the floor it is judged by) and the round-5 security tests are listed by name. Added in the security loop (round 6): the exact external-script allowlist the published-artifact gate enforces (src/validators/external-script-allowlist.ts: host and path of the analytics loader are pinned there, only the GA4 id comes from src/config/analytics.ts); its test and the other round-6 tests sit under tests/security/**. Added in the security loop (round 7): scripts/security-alert.ts, the host CLI that sends security alerts through the deadman's email and notification path (it mails as the owner, and the host integrity check calls it); its shared email transport and the deadman's signal-source module sit under src/watchdog/**, and the round-7 tests under tests/security/**. Added in the security loop (round 8): the publish-trust modules and everything the publish-trust roots import directly (src/validators/published-artifacts.ts, src/generators/security-headers.ts, src/utils/safe-url.ts, scripts/save-batch.ts): the search-engine ownership-proof allowlist (src/validators/verification-allowlist.ts), the GA4 id (src/config/analytics.ts), the ticket-URL trust decision and its inputs (src/ticketing/ticket-trust.ts, validator.ts, venue-registry.ts, src/utils/ticket-source-classifier.ts), the URL-column module scripts/lib/url-columns.ts wraps (src/db/url-columns.ts), the site origin (src/config/site-url.ts) and the enrichment gates save-batch applies (src/utils/tag-filter.ts, src/enrichment/quality-gates.ts, word-counter.ts, description-generator.ts, enrichment-matrix.ts); tests/security/publish-trust-protected.test.ts fails when one of those roots imports a module this list does not cover (some exist only on the regular branch and are listed ahead of the merge). Also the host jobs that read the container-written events.db, now only through the untrusted-DB reader, and that reader's CLI (scripts/untrusted-db-query.ts, scripts/daily-enrichment-check.sh, scripts/weekly-digest.ts, scripts/monitor-search-visibility.ts; the reader itself sits under src/watchdog/**), the default-branch config reader .github/scripts/default-branch-file.sh (listed by name although .github/** covers it) and the ruleset-check test tests/branch-rules-check.test.ts. Added in the security loop (round 9): scripts/run-tests.sh, the documented `bun run test` runner that passes bun an explicit test list and refuses test files planted in container-writable folders (a plain `bun test` would run them on the Mac); scripts/phase1-exit-gate.ts, which the weekly digest runs on the Mac and which now reads the container-written events.db and deploy-cadence.log only through the untrusted-DB reader and the bounded no-follow log reader.
